$comment: Registry for issue #834's CI-enforced mutation gate.
Each entry describes ONE mutant: a small, reviewable patch against exactly one
production file, plus the test filter that MUST turn red when the patch is applied
(the 'exploit'/detection filter) and the test filter that MUST stay green (the
positive control, proving the harness itself still works and the mutation did not
have broader collateral effects than declared).
kind:
security  - a real mutant against production security-fix code. Run by the main
'mutants' job in .github/workflows/mutation-gate.yml. A non-KILLED
verdict on ANY security-kind entry is ALWAYS a gate failure -- there is
no per-entry override. That is intentional: this registry is a forcing
function, not a place to declare a known-broken test 'expected' and move
on (that is precisely the loophole issue #834 exists to close).
selftest  - a meta-fixture used only to test the runner (run_mutant.py) itself, e.g.
to prove a non-compiling patch is reported as an invalid mutant and never
as a pass. Run by the separate 'meta-selftest' job, invoked with
--expect-verdict so the *runner's own correctness* is what is asserted,
not any real security property. selftest entries are never mixed into the
main gate's pass/fail decision.
red_expected_assertion_patterns maps each red_tests[] fully-qualified test name to a
regex that MUST match that test's MSTest failure message for the kill to count. This is
what stops rule-of-thumb 'non-zero exit = detected': a test that goes red with an
unrelated NullReferenceException or a fixture crash does not match and is reported as
UNEXPECTED_RED (gate failure), not KILLED.

mutants.description: Empties the UpdateModelProperty inline-edit sensitive-field blocklist (compile-preserving operator: HashSet literal emptied, not deleted) and checks it against the HTTP-layer MvcAuthHolesTests that guard MVC-004's blockedFields HashSet specifically: Password and ITCode. HISTORY: as originally filed for issue #834, these tests used StudentListVM (a ListVM) and a fake Guid id, so `vm as IBaseCRUDVM<TopBasePoco>` was null and _FrameworkController.cs:540 returned the same 400 ('Entity not found') whether or not the blocklist existed -- this entry's red filter used to include the dot-notation test too and the whole set SURVIVED, which was the demonstration issue #834 asked for (see PR #839 history for that transcript). Issue #837 (PR #845, merged as f148a1383) rewrote the fixture to seed a real FrameworkUser via a real CRUD VM (FrameworkUserVM) and assert on the endpoint's own custom message text, so Password and ITCode now correctly reach the blockedFields check and this entry is KILLED. UpdateModelProperty_DotNotationField_ReturnsBadRequest was removed from this entry's red_tests: it pins a DIFFERENT, earlier, unconditional guard (`field.Contains('.')` at _FrameworkController.cs:513) that emptying blockedFields has no bearing on -- see mvc004-dotnotation-guard-neutralize below for its own mutant. It remains in this entry's green_tests instead, as a positive control proving emptying blockedFields has no effect on that sibling guard.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.MvcAuthHolesTes: MVC-004: Password field must be blocked\. Got 200\.
MVC-004: ITCode field must be blocked\. Got 200\.

mutants.red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first -- see run_mutant.py's clean_stale_demo_db, added after this exact capture was corrupted by leftover row state on the first attempt) with the mutant patch applied and #845's fixture in place: 'Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<BadRequest>. Actual:<OK>. MVC-004: Password field must be blocked. Got 200.' and 'Assert.AreEqual failed. Expected:<BadRequest>. Actual:<OK>. MVC-004: ITCode field must be blocked. Got 200.' respectively.

mutants.description: Neutralizes the dot-notation traversal guard at _FrameworkController.cs:513-516 (`if (field.Contains('.')) return BadRequest("Navigation property paths are not allowed for inline editing");`) with a compile-preserving operator (`field.Contains('.') && false`, not a deletion) so the condition can never be true. Checked against UpdateModelProperty_DotNotationField_ReturnsBadRequest, which submits field="Photo.FileName" against a real seeded FrameworkUser. With the guard neutralized, the request still returns 400 -- 'Photo.FileName' is not a legal CLR member name, so it falls through to the unrelated property-existence check a few lines later (_FrameworkController.cs, `entityType.GetProperty(field, ...)` returning null) and gets 'Field not found or not writable' instead. Status-code-only assertions cannot tell those two 400s apart; the test's second assertion (the response body must contain 'Navigation property paths are not allowed') is what actually pins this guard, and is exactly what goes red here. green_tests are UpdateModelProperty_PasswordField_ReturnsBadRequest and UpdateModelProperty_ITCodeField_ReturnsBadRequest, proving blast-radius scoping in the other direction from mvc004-blocklist-empty-http-blindspot: neutralizing the dot-notation guard has no effect on the independent blockedFields check.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Api.Test.MvcAuthHolesTes: the 400 must come from the dot-notation guard specifically.*Got body: Field not found or not writable

mutants.red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout with the mutant patch applied: 'Assert.IsTrue failed. MVC-004: the 400 must come from the dot-notation guard specifically (its message), not from the unrelated property-existence check that would ALSO 400 a literal "Photo.FileName" property lookup if the dot-notation guard were deleted. Got body: Field not found or not writable'.

mutants.description: The SAME production patch as mvc004-blocklist-empty-http-blindspot, checked instead against test/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Admin.Test/FrameworkControllerUpdateModelPropertyPersistTests.cs's UpdateModelProperty_BlockedField_StillRejectedAndNotPersisted, which calls _FrameworkController.UpdateModelProperty directly against a real BaseCRUDVM<Major> and a real seeded row. This entry is included specifically to prove the runner's KILLED path (red-for-the-expected-reason) is exercised against real production code in this same PR, not merely implemented and never run: the same mutation that the HTTP-layer tests structurally cannot see IS caught here, because this test reaches the actual guarded code path.

mutants.description: Meta test for the runner itself (issue #834 acceptance criterion: 'gate 本身有一支 meta 測試：invalid mutant（編譯失敗）不得被判為通過'). The patch introduces a deliberate C# syntax error next to the same blockedFields symbol. Proves run_mutant.py treats a non-compiling patch as an invalid mutant / gate FAILURE, never a pass -- run_mutant.py --expect-verdict is used to assert on the runner's own verdict, not on any real security behaviour. Never included in the main 'mutants' job.
